answer: Stake-ladder issuance with rate limiting blocks sybil floods. Step one: an applicant locks 250 POA in a contract with a 30-day unlock. Step two: it mints one non-transferable identity token per address. Step three: each further identity costs four times the last, so a second costs 1,000 POA and a fifth 64,000. Step four: any proven clone is slashed and blacklisted. A thousand clones would demand more POA than the chain will ever mint. It is like a prism: one honest identity fans into a clean beam, while clone armies smear the same ledge into umber, each smear costing four times the last.
